policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 126:4 'Turn again our captivity' renders the noun with 1cp suffix; qere שְׁבִיתֵנוּ and ketiv שבותנו are orthographic variants of the same word (shebith/shebuth, 'captivity') with identical sense and suffix, so the English cannot distinguish them. No textual note on the verse. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
